title: Staged change consequences scratch - Jaya
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for thinking through the downstream consequences of small, staged changes (canary -> ramp -> full). Intended to be messy, with TODOs and questions to resolve before rolling beyond canary.

Top-level hypothesis:
- Make many small changes safer by enumerating non-obvious stateful interactions that can cause silent regressions (KV cache invalidation, batching heuristics, kernel selection toggles).

Immediate context / triggers:
- PR 1428 touches the KV cache eviction timing and adds a tiny heuristic to prefetch prefixes for repeated short-context requests.
- Load tests on dedicated env show ~3% median latency improvement but 0.4% tail regressions under bursty traffic.
- INF-3342 flagged by SRE: unexplained increase in transient 503s during ramp tests.

Quick checklist before ramping past 10%:
- [ ] Reproduce 503 locally with recorded traces from the canary region (ask SRE for trace IDs).
- [ ] Confirm prefetch path is strictly opt-in via config flag; ensure default off in Dedicated existing customers unless explicitly migrated.
- [ ] Add metric for "kv-prefetch-prefilled" vs "kv-prefetch-miss" so we can correlate misses to 503 spikes.
- [ ] Add a short TTL boundary test (1s, 10s, 60s) to unit tests for eviction edge cases.
- [ ] Run chaos test: sudden goroutine restarts while many small requests are in-flight to exercise KV concurrency.
- [ ] Evaluate impact on batching: does prefetch increase the variance of token computation time and therefore increase batching timeouts?

Notes / hypotheses about root cause (brain dump):
- Hypothesis A: prefetch increases memory pressure (temporary objects), causing GC pauses in certain languages/runtimes -> spikes in request handling time -> perceivable 503s when queue backlog hits timeout.
- Hypothesis B: prefetch code path races with evictions; under bursty patterns a prefix is prefetched then immediately evicted leading to extra work and a partial failure path that surfaces as 503.
- Hypothesis C: new heuristic touches kernel selection table and under some micro-architectures picks a less-robust kernel path causing intermittent failures for long sequences. (low probability but worth checking if kernel selection mapping used by runtime was mutated)

Quick experiments to run (cheap, quick feedback):
- Local microbench harness: replay 10m short requests with and without prefetch; capture GC/alloc profiles.
- Synthetic canary: 2 replicas with prefetch enabled; route 1% of traffic and inject burst patterns (sudden 10x short requests for 30s).
- Feature-flagged rollout: add kill-switch that disables prefetch immediately and validates reduction in 503s. Test kill-switch script end-to-end.

Observability additions (minimal to be useful):
- New metrics: kv_prefetch_attempts, kv_prefetch_hits, kv_prefetch_evictions, kv_prefetch_alloc_bytes.
- Trace spans: mark prefetch start/end, mark eviction decision. Tag traces with config flags and kernel selection id.
- Alert rule (temporary during ramp): if region 5m error rate increases >0.2% absolute after enabling prefetch and prefetch_hits < 80% => auto-disable and page.

Refactor follow-ups (post-mitigation cleanups):
- Consolidate prefetch logic into a single small module with clear sync boundaries to avoid scattered locking patterns.
- Extract a test harness for eviction windows so other features can reuse it.
- Add documentation snippet in Serving Runtime README describing prefetch tradeoffs and intended workloads.

Questions I want answered before full rollout (open):
- Is there any customer workload where prefetch would materially increase cost due to extra KV writes or memory churn? (billing impact)
- What is the interaction with caching layers upstream (edge cache)? Could we be double-caching and causing wasted cycles?
- Are there specific hardware types (A100 vs H100 vs CPU-only) where the kernel choice induced by the prefetch path is problematic?

Slack pings to send (templates):
- To SRE: "sre-team quick check: can you share trace IDs for spikes in region-us-west-2 between 2025-02-25 11:03–11:07 UTC? suspect KV prefetch path; want spans including kernel-selection tags."
- To Runtime Eng: "runtime folks: PR 1428 prefetch change shows tail regressions under burst. Can someone validate kernel-selection table hasn't been changed inadvertently? ping @LiamChen @AshaRao"

Decision matrix (simple):
- If prefetch_hits >= 90% and no tail increase in 99th latency -> continue ramp.
- If prefetch_hits between 60-90% and small tail changes (<5% relative) -> hold at 10% and add observability improvements.
- If prefetch_hits < 60% or tail latency increases >5% or errors increase -> rollback immediately.

Short autopsy notes template (if we need to roll back):
- What was the roll forward window and % traffic?
- Which metrics deviated first (latency, errors, gc, allocs)?
- Which config flag toggles were in place? Who approved?
- Root cause hypothesis and concrete follow-up owners (list owners + tickets).

Thing-to-remember (random small heuristics):
- Prefer feature-flags with timeouts (auto-disable after X minutes of elevated errors) for experiments touching shared state.
- Name metrics with the "prefetch" prefix so debugging filter is easy.
- Keep canary cohorts small and geographically co-located to avoid cross-region network noise.

Followups (action items with owners):
- Jaya: add kv_prefetch metrics and a lightweight unit test for eviction timing (INF-3401).
- Liam Chen: run local replay and share GC/alloc profiles in the thread (due 2025-02-14).
- Asha Rao: instrument trace spans in PR 1428 and push a canary image to staging (due 2025-02-15).

Loose notes / scribbles:
- If prefetch helps short conversational workloads a lot, maybe we gate it by route type (small backends like chat-short).
- Consider dynamic TTL: if prefix used > N times in T window, extend TTL; else let eviction follow normal rules. Need to weigh complexity vs benefit.
- Could we leverage the existing cache-warming job instead of inline prefetch to avoid latency spikes?

End of scratchpad. Will iterate once I get traces and the replay data.

Unresolved: ask legal about adding debug traces that may contain user prompts — need to ensure traces scrub PII before storing.
